user.title: Find the heat pump
user.description:
Search the network asks every address on Home Assistant's own private networks, on port 80, whether it is a CTC display, and changes nothing anywhere; a network of public addresses is never searched. Enter an address skips the search, and is also the way in for a display whose web interface is switched off.

From the start, control of the heat pump, the walk to System information, the anonymous statistics and the check for new releases are switched on; all four are changed under Configure. What the statistics send: {privacy_url}

scan.title: Choose heat pump
scan.description: CTC displays found on Home Assistant's own networks: {count}. Addresses that are already set up are left out.

manual.title: Enter address
manual.description: Type the display's address. It is shown on the panel under Installer, Settings, Communication, Ethernet. Where the display's web interface does not answer, the heat pump is added on Modbus alone: no display pages, no coefficient of performance and no serial number, until the web interface is turned on and the menu is read again under Configure.

modbus_failed.title: Modbus does not answer
modbus_failed.description: The display at {host} answers, but Modbus does not. Turn it on at the panel under Installer, Define, Remote control, where Ethernet must be set to Modbus TCP; the port row only appears once that is done. Then try again, with the same address or a corrected one.

modbus_busy.title: Modbus is taken
modbus_busy.description: The heat pump at {host} accepts a connection on its Modbus port and drops it as soon as anything is asked. The controller takes one Modbus client at a time, and another one holds the place: usually a modbus: block in configuration.yaml pointing at the same unit, a test tool, or a connection that was never let go and that the controller still believes is there. Remove the other client, wait ten minutes, and try again.

slow.title: Slow values from the display
slow.description:
Modbus is read continuously and handles all control. The display's web interface additionally carries values Modbus does not have, such as delivered heat.

The catch is that only the page the panel is showing stays fresh, so the integration has to walk there and back. The panel moves while it does. Tick the pages you want, or skip this step and run on Modbus alone.

The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data, where delivered heat is counted.

{count} pages were found on the {model}; the figure after each is how many values it holds.

From the start, control of the heat pump, the walk to System information, the anonymous statistics and the check for new releases are switched on; all four are changed under Configure. What the statistics send: {privacy_url}

confirm.title: Add {model}?
confirm.description:
A CTC display was found at {host}. Setting it up walks the unit's menu to see what it can report, so the panel will move for a moment.

From the start, control of the heat pump, the walk to System information, the anonymous statistics and the check for new releases are switched on; all four are changed under Configure. What the statistics send: {privacy_url}

error.not_a_ctc: That address does not answer as a CTC display. Check the address. The display's web interface is turned on at the panel under Installer, Define, Communication, Web = Yes; without it the heat pump is added on Modbus alone, and then Modbus has to answer.
error.modbus_failed: Modbus did not answer this time either.
error.modbus_transient: Modbus did not answer a moment ago and answers now, so it was a passing hiccup. Try again.
error.modbus_rejected: Something answers on that Modbus TCP port, but not as the heat pump: with a Modbus error, or as a device that does not speak Modbus at all. Check the Modbus TCP port, 502 unless it was changed at the panel, and the Modbus address, normally 1.
error.nothing_found: The search found no CTC display. Type the display's address instead; a display on another network is not reached by the search.
error.only_configured: The search found only displays that are already set up. To add another heat pump, type its display's address; a display on another network is not reached by the search.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: This heat pump is already being added. Finish it from its card under Discovered in Settings, Devices and services, or wait for the other set-up to end.
abort.not_a_ctc: The device is not a CTC display.

data.visit_system_info: Let the integration open System information on the panel
data.check_updates: Tell me when a new version is released

data_description.enable_control: Creates control entities that write to CTC's volatile 1000 registers. The controller forgets them about five minutes after the last write, so control releases itself if Home Assistant stops. The stored settings in the 61500 block are never written.
data_description.send_statistics: One report per day to {endpoint}: the integration's version, the Home Assistant version, installation type and Python version, the language and the country you configured in Home Assistant, an approximate position rounded to about 11 km, the number of entities and devices, which transports are in use, whether control is enabled, how many display pages are harvested, how many pages the display's menu has and whether the last reading of the menu since Home Assistant started recognised the home screen and got into the operation data menu, whether the row with the unit's operating hours was recognised on the history page, whether the counters behind the coefficient of performance were found on the display or in Modbus and whether each handed over a number at the last read, and when there is no figure, why: too little energy counted so far, a counter standing still although the unit has been running, or a quotient no heat pump could produce. Also the number of failed register reads, the indoor and outdoor unit's model, for an indoor unit the integration does not know yet the family code in the name of the display's settings file (such as ezi3xx, two to sixteen lowercase letters and digits, nothing else), the firmware in the display, the heat pump's control board and the control unit, the product and the year and week of manufacture from the serial number, and the coefficient of performance (COP) over the last day, a rolling year, the machine's first year and the lifetime. One measurement leaves the house, and only when it is wrong: where a counter stands still or the two counters give an impossible quotient, the two lifetime totals in kilowatt hours are sent along with the flag, never otherwise. Never a name, an address, an exact position, a full serial number, an entity name or a page name, never anything finer than one day, and your IP address is not stored. It also sends a random id created when the integration was installed, so that the daily reports can be kept apart and erased on request (the server keeps it only as a hash, and it says nothing about who you are), a hash that links the beolink plugins running on the same Home Assistant, how many warnings and errors the integration logged since the previous report, and whether it is running or waiting to start again, never the messages themselves or the reason. Switching this off also erases what has already been sent. The full list: {privacy_url}
data_description.visit_system_info: The panel walks to the display's System information page once and back, to read the serial number and the display's own software version. It presses nothing but Advanced, Display and System information, checks where the panel went after every press, and gives up at the first surprise.
data_description.check_updates: Asks GitHub once a day whether a newer release of this integration exists, and says so in the repairs view. Home Assistant only offers updates for what HACS installed, so a copy put in place by hand is otherwise never offered one.
data_description.slow_pages: The figure after each page is how many values it holds.

rescan.title: Slow values from the display
rescan.description: {count} pages were found. The panel was moved during the scan and put back. The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data. The figure after each page is how many values it holds.

abort.panel_busy: The panel is in use right now: the integration is reading the display's pages or walking its menu. Try again in a moment. Nothing has been changed.

pages_unticked.title: No page of the display is ticked
pages_unticked.description: The display's menu has been read, but not one of its pages is ticked, so the display is never read: delivered heat, and with it the coefficient of performance, lives only there. Tick the pages under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure. The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data.

menu_unread.title: The display's menu could not be read
menu_unread.description: No page of the display is read, because its menu could not be read: the integration did not find its way from the home screen into the operation data menu, or the display did not answer. Until then only Modbus is read, without delivered heat or a coefficient of performance. The menu is tried again three times, five minutes apart, after every start of Home Assistant, and at once with Read the display's menu again under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure. If it never works, download the diagnostics from the integration's menu and attach them to an issue on GitHub: they show how far the reading got.

history_page_missing.title: The coefficient of performance is missing its history page
history_page_missing.description: The coefficient of performance is worked out from the display's counter for delivered heat, which lives on the page with the stored or historical operation data. That page is not being read. Tick it under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure.

identity_incomplete.title: The serial number has not been read
identity_incomplete.description: The display writes the serial number and its own software version into the System information page only once that page has been shown on the panel. Open it once on the panel, or let the integration walk there itself under Configure.

modbus_busy.title: Another client holds the heat pump's Modbus connection
modbus_busy.description: The controller takes one Modbus client at a time. It accepts this integration's connection and drops it as soon as anything is asked, which is how it says that another client holds the place: a modbus: block in configuration.yaml pointing at the same unit, a test tool, or a session that was never let go. Remove the other client and wait ten minutes. The integration keeps trying by itself, and this notice goes at the first reading that works.

update_available.title: A newer version of CTC Local Easyconf is out
update_available.description: Version {latest} has been released; this is {installed}. Installed through HACS: update it there, under Settings, Devices and services, HACS. Installed by hand: replace custom_components/ctc_ecozenith with the new release and restart Home Assistant.

modbus_busy.message: Another client holds the heat pump's only Modbus connection; see the repairs view

modbus_closed.message: The heat pump does not accept a connection on its Modbus port: it is switched off or out of reach, the address is wrong, or Modbus TCP is off at the panel
